Subject: Coordinating model refactor windows + comms playbook (ask: carve-outs & SLA language)

Team —

We need a short cross-functional plan for the upcoming model refactor that starts in mid-Oct. The two asks up front:

1) Product asks: a clear matrix of incompatibilities (API surface, embedding dimension changes, tokenization drift) that we can present to customers so they can self-assess.

2) Comms/contract asks: a recommended carve-out language for customers still on legacy endpoints, and a proposed SLA fallback during the cutover (72h extended window for critical customers).

I'd like a one-pager + CSV impact matrix we can share with pilot customers by 2026-09-10. Ben — please own the CSV impact matrix and tag the highest-risk customers. Marissa — draft the customer comms and optional 'temporary pin' instructions we can include for Dedicated/Private installs. Karthik & Grace — engineering/ops, confirm technical feasibility for the 72h rollback/fallback and any monitoring hooks we need exposed in Console.

Quick timeline suggestion:
- 2026-09-03: internal sign-off on impact matrix + comm draft
- 2026-09-10: pilot customer outreach (5–8 customers)
- 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18: planned refactor window (region-by-region)

Attachments: migration-impact-matrix.csv (draft), refactor-windows-slides.pdf

Thanks — Logan

[Signature]
Logan Wright
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Logan —

I've started the CSV and populated an initial risk column. Highlights:
- Tokenization differences: 14 customers (mostly NLP analytics) flagged as high risk.
- Embedding dimension change: affects two major customers on Dedicated; we should offer an "embedding-compat shim" for 30 days.
- API param renames: low risk (doced), can be handled with a deprecation header for 60 days.

I attached a first pass. I also recommend we surface a per-customer recommended action: Accept refactor, Adopt shim, or Request migration support.

Attachment: migration-impact-matrix.csv (CSV, 48 KB)

Ben

Thanks team — draft comms attached. Two versions: short notice (pilot outreach) and full notice (general availability).

Key points in draft:
- What is changing (concise bullets + example curl requests)
- Migration options (auto-shim, manual pin to legacy endpoint, migration support engagement)
- Safety net: 72h rollback guarantee for pilot customers; for GA customers, we propose a 14-day soft-deprecation with extended support on request.

Open questions for legal/sales language (Ben, can you flag customers who need explicit contractual carve-outs?).

Attachment: customer-comm-drafts.docx (DOCX, 22 KB)

-Marissa

Quick engineering check: the 72h rollback guarantee is feasible but requires two things from product/CS: (1) a list of explicitly opted-in pilot customers so we can pre-provision fallback capacity, and (2) a single-point contact on-call during the refactor window to approve emergency rollbacks. Without that, rollback adds non-trivial ops overhead.

We will add a Console flag to mark "pilot/rollback-eligible" instances; Grace will sketch the UX, and I can wire the backend. Also: embedding-compat shim is doable as an adapter layer (cost estimate attached).

Cost note: pre-provisioned fallback capacity increases reserved GPU costs by ~6% for the week — flagging for finance.

Karthik
